mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS increased by more than 0.25% in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced consumer spending and economic slowdown.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of the instances where UNRATE increased by more than 0.5% in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP growth over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations adjust downward.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of the periods following two consecutive quarters of declining GDPC1.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 1% in a month signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as increased production capacity supports economic growth.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where INDPRO increased by more than 1% in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is above 4% and the CPI is increasing by more than 0.3% per month, the combination signals a high inflation environment with tight monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increase > 0.3% in 1 month
regime_hint: high inflation with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increased by more than 0.3% in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in nonfarm payrolls by more than 100,000 in a month signals a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced economic activity.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of the instances where PAYEMS decreased by more than 100,000 in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts by more than 10% over two months signals a strengthening demand environment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as increased construction activity supports economic growth.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of the periods following a 10% increase in HOUST over two months.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (PCE) increase by more than 1% in a month and the unemployment rate decreases by more than 0.2%, the combination signals a strengthening demand environment with an improving labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increase > 1% in 1 month and UNRATE decrease > 0.2% in 1 month
regime_hint: early-cycle expansion with improving labor market
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where RSAFS increased by more than 1% and UNRATE decreased by more than 0.2% in the prior month.
